title: Schizophrenia negative symptom: decreased facial expressiveness (flat affect)
vignette: A 27-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by her employer due to increasingly paranoid and disorganized behavior over the past year. The patient works as a housekeeper and has had progressive difficulty performing her work responsibilities. She has become increasingly secretive over the past 6 months and recently started talking in a whisper because she believes that listening devices are planted in the walls. Over the past month, she started hiding food and personal possessions in closets and under beds. The patient does not use alcohol or illicit drugs. Vital signs are stable, and physical examination is unremarkable. During the interview, she changes topics frequently and rambles about voices harassing her. Which of the following additional mental status findings is most likely in this patient?

clues.text: increasingly paranoid and disorganized behavior over the past year
clues.note: More than 6 months of psychosis with functional decline meets the duration criterion for schizophrenia (vs a brief psychotic disorder or schizophreniform disorder).

clues.text: believes that listening devices are planted in the walls
clues.note: A fixed persecutory delusion is a POSITIVE symptom of schizophrenia.

clues.text: changes topics frequently and rambles about voices harassing her
clues.note: Disorganized/tangential speech plus auditory hallucinations are additional POSITIVE symptoms - auditory hallucinations are the most common type in schizophrenia.

whatMatters: A >1-year course of delusions, auditory hallucinations, disorganized speech, and functional decline = schizophrenia. Beyond positive symptoms, patients also have NEGATIVE symptoms - flat affect shown as DECREASED FACIAL EXPRESSIVENESS (plus monotone voice, poor eye contact). Answer A. Negative symptoms persist between episodes and respond poorly to antipsychotics.
strategy: Confirm schizophrenia (>=2 symptoms, >=6 months, functional decline), then predict the co-occurring finding. The stem already lists POSITIVE symptoms; the 'additional' finding is a NEGATIVE symptom -> flat affect = decreased facial expressiveness (A). Reject items that belong to other disorders: euphoria/pressured speech = mania; fluctuating consciousness = delirium; olfactory/tactile hallucinations = organic/substance causes.

eliminations.label: Euphoric mood - mania
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: elevated/expansive mood characteristic of a manic episode (bipolar disorder). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it's not a feature of schizophrenia. ✅ Correct if: mania with decreased need for sleep and grandiosity.

eliminations.label: Fluctuating level of consciousness - delirium
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a waxing-waning sensorium is the hallmark of DELIRIUM. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: schizophrenia patients are alert and oriented with a stable sensorium. ✅ Correct if: acute waxing-waning attention from a medical cause.

eliminations.label: Olfactory hallucinations - organic/seizure
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: smelling things that aren't there, suggesting a neurologic cause (e.g., temporal lobe seizure aura). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: uncommon in schizophrenia, whose hallucinations are predominantly auditory. ✅ Correct if: a seizure aura or organic lesion.

eliminations.label: Pressured speech - mania
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: rapid, hard-to-interrupt speech seen in mania. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: schizophrenic speech is disorganized (tangential/derailed) but not typically pressured. ✅ Correct if: a manic episode.

eliminations.label: Tactile hallucinations - substance/delirium, your pick
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: sensations of things on/under the skin (e.g., cocaine 'formication'). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: tactile hallucinations point to substance use or delirium; schizophrenia's hallucinations are mostly auditory, and the MOST likely additional finding is a negative symptom (flat affect). ✅ Correct if: stimulant intoxication/withdrawal or delirium.

reasoning: >1 year of delusions, auditory hallucinations, disorganized speech, and functional decline = schizophrenia
Schizophrenia includes NEGATIVE symptoms alongside positive ones
Flat affect manifests on exam as decreased facial expressiveness (+ monotone voice, poor eye contact)
mechanism: Schizophrenia is diagnosed by two or more symptom domains (delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, disorganized/catatonic behavior, negative symptoms) for at least 6 months with significant functional decline. Symptoms are grouped as POSITIVE (delusions, hallucinations - characteristically auditory - and disorganization, all present here) and NEGATIVE (flat/blunted affect, avolition, alogia, anhedonia, asociality). Flat affect is manifested on mental status examination as DECREASED FACIAL EXPRESSIVENESS, a monotone voice, and poor eye contact; negative symptoms tend to persist between acute psychotic episodes and respond less well to antipsychotic medication. Euphoria and pressured speech indicate mania, a fluctuating level of consciousness indicates delirium, and olfactory/tactile hallucinations point to neurologic or substance-related causes rather than schizophrenia.

difficulty.label: 🧲 Pulled by a distractor
difficulty.message: Your pick (tactile hallucinations) suggests substance/delirium; B/E are mania; C is delirium; D is organic. Auditory is the schizophrenia hallucination type.

difficulty.label: ✍️ Something else
difficulty.message: Bank: schizophrenia = positive (delusions, auditory hallucinations, disorganization) + negative (flat affect = decreased facial expressiveness), which persist between episodes.
